speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Deforming the Poisson bracket
summary: The introductory announcement of Polyakov's physics lectures is followed by Kirillov's report of Vey's deformation theorem. The page distinguishes local finite-order brackets from formal bidifferential deformations, and ends with the suggestive relation \(pq-qp=t\). The displayed planar formula suppresses necessary mixed derivatives; its omission is mathematical shorthand or error in the notebook, not an error introduced by translation.

speaker: A. M. Polyakov
title: Spinors, gauge invariance, and perturbative quantum electrodynamics
summary: This extended introductory lecture moves from the particle table to Weyl and Dirac fields, local phase covariance, electromagnetic connections, propagators, Feynman parameters, and charge screening. Gelfand's Gaussian-integral analogy interrupts the discussion. The notebook combines exact finite-dimensional identities with formal functional integrals and schematic diagrams; the companion preserves that distinction.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Essentially normal operators and extension classes
summary: Gelfand reports the Brown--Douglas--Fillmore classification and its connection with odd \(K\)-homology, under a heading mentioning Atiyah. Essential normality and the equivalence relation defining \(\operatorname{Ext}\) are omitted in the shorthand. The intervening line ``Moser---Korteweg--de Vries'' contains no mathematical assertion and receives no separate item.

speaker: B. Kostant
title: Euler products, root systems, and Kostant’s character formula
summary: The Euler product and its familiar powers introduce the Macdonald identities and Kostant's character-theoretic form. Manin anticipates his next discussion of several expressions for \(\tau(n)\), and Gelfand asks only the suggestive question \(\psi(x)^z\). The spectral-zeta fragment is too compressed to identify a unique formula.

speaker: A. M. Polyakov
title: From lepton symmetries to electroweak gauge fields
summary: After reading recommendations, Polyakov extends the QED construction to chiral lepton doublets and local \(SU(2)\) symmetry. Charged currents, muon decay, neutral-field mixing, and the then four-flavour, three-colour quark count appear. The Higgs sector and hypercharge assignment are not supplied in these pages; a complete electroweak reconstruction must mark those additions.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: The Lie algebra of differential polynomials
summary: Gelfand introduces the bracket on differential polynomials underlying evolutionary equations and the KdV hierarchy. Povzner identifies its action by derivations. On the same page Manin's opening definition of \(\tau\) precedes the Gelfand passage and his numbered formulas follow it; the catalogue's two Manin records are therefore kept distinct.

speaker: Yu. I. Manin
title: Opening definition of Ramanujan’s tau function
summary: This catalogue record is represented by the short Manin heading and product definition at the top of P000613. Gelfand's differential-polynomial discussion follows immediately; Manin resumes below it in record 370. The mathematical content is therefore one definition, despite the archive's broad overlapping page range.

speaker: Yu. I. Manin
title: Eight descriptions of Ramanujan’s tau function
summary: Manin resumes with a list announced as six expressions but numbered through eight: the product, Dyson's root-lattice sum, divisor convolutions, lattice theta series, a period formula, partition asymptotics, Hecke multiplicativity, and a Galois representation. The subsequent explanation invokes eta transformations, the ring of modular forms, Rademacher contours, and Kostant's identity. Several formulas are faithfully transcribed mathematical errors; their corrected forms and the exact scope of independent finite checks are separated from the notebook.

speaker: J. Leray
title: Quadratic Fourier operators and the metaplectic group
summary: Leray explains the algebraic background of Maslov's method, beginning with the Schwartz space, its distribution dual, and linear position--momentum operators. Quadratic generating functions produce unitary integral operators. The notes then pass from their arbitrary scalar phases to the metaplectic double cover and its Maslov signs; this passage needs a phase convention beyond unitarity alone. The subject continues the metaplectic discussion in 1973-312.1--2 and 1973-315.1--4.

speaker: E. S. Fradkin
title: Integrable particle systems and constrained quantization
summary: After Fradkin's reading list, Perelomov gives a substantial intervening report on Toda and Calogero--Moser systems. Its table distinguishes finding conserved quantities, proving their involution, reconstructing the dynamics, and performing quadratures; elliptic involution and exceptional root systems are explicitly questioned. Gelfand asks about a larger group-theoretic construction. Fradkin then returns to Bose and Fermi canonical variables, constrained Hamiltonian systems, and a formal functional integral. The individual attributions below follow the page headings rather than assigning Perelomov's report to Fradkin.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Fractional differential operators and stationary KdV
summary: Gelfand introduces Krichever's report by recalling the differential parts of fractional Schrödinger powers and the stationary one-gap equation. His final suggestion of an unworked-out noncommutative theory remains a programme rather than a precise conjecture. This brief intervention continues the higher-KdV discussion of 1973 and the finite-gap work of 1974.

speaker: I. M. Krichever
title: Algebraic curves and commuting ordinary differential operators
summary: Krichever passes from coefficient equations for commuting scalar operators to their algebraic spectral curve, then reverses the construction using a normalized Baker--Akhiezer function. The report includes the polynomial-relation theorem attributed to Shabat, pole-order gaps, a genus criterion, a centralizer intervention, and a theta formula. Several distinctions matter: algebraic dependence was known earlier; rank-one spectral data are required for the scalar eigenfunction construction; a pole divisor is a bound rather than an exact divisor at every \(x\); and the claimed algebraic independence and final theta normalization contain errors. The notebook's date is retained even though Krichever's 1977 retrospective mentions related seminar talks in November--December 1975.

speaker: B. A. Dubrovin
title: Matrix finite-gap operators and Jacobians
summary: The dated heading on P000625 begins Dubrovin's talk; P000623--P000624 continue Krichever's preceding talk. Dubrovin constructs matrix hierarchies, reduces their stationary equations to a polynomial matrix Lax equation, and identifies generic isospectral sets with a diagonal-group bundle over a Jacobian. The actual mathematical span is P000625--P000626. A sign reversal in the commutator equation is a notebook error, not a change of convention that can consistently be retained.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Geometry and mathematical preparation for physicists
summary: The heading and informal lecture occur on P000627, continuing at the top of P000628 before Polyakov begins. An ant on a cube motivates curvature and torsion, followed by a programme for geometry and relativity on lattices, a physics reading list, and mathematics proposed for physicists. Bare subject names are recorded as a curriculum remark rather than converted into nonexistent conjectures.

speaker: A. M. Polyakov
title: Quark representations, color and the Wilson-loop confinement problem
summary: Polyakov begins on P000628 after Gelfand's reading programme and finishes on P000630. The discussion moves from hadron representations and quark statistics to color gauge invariance, infinitely heavy probes, rectangular Wilson loops and a Gaussian Abelian comparison. Representation identities, phenomenological approximations, established constructions and the unsolved four-dimensional confinement question are separated. A reference to the penultimate issue of \emph{Theoretical and Mathematical Physics} lacks an author, title or year sufficiently specific to identify a paper.

title: Year heading: 1976
summary: This catalogue record marks the change of calendar year. Its overlapping page links include the end of the November 1975 discussion and the dated 9 February 1976 talk, but provide no independent mathematical assertion. It receives zero occurrence items; all following item identifiers retain academic-year prefix 1975.

speaker: I. M. Krichever
title: Baker-Akhiezer construction of Zakharov-Shabat equations
summary: The dated talk occupies P000631--P000632 and the first two lines of P000633. It passes from formal exponential solutions to algebraic spectral data and the uniqueness argument constructing differential operators. Gelfand asks an elementary commuting-operator problem and raises the distinction between a formal series and an analytic function. Drinfeld begins a separate algebraization immediately below on P000633.

speaker: V. G. Drinfeld
title: Algebraization by filtered modules
summary: Drinfeld begins beneath the end of Krichever's proof on P000633 and continues through P000634. He replaces an embedding of the punctured-curve function ring into differential operators by a filtered module and a connection-like operator. Gelfand's reciprocity and division-ring remarks are preserved as separate, underspecified programmes. The construction directly anticipates Drinfeld's 1977 note, which acknowledges the seminar context.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Brodskii radial spectral inversion; Fuchs on characteristic cycles
summary: P000635 explicitly describes Novikov reporting work of M. Brodskii of Minsk; the matching author is M. A. Brodskii. The radial spectral problem, semiclassical action and Abel inversion match his 1976 two-page note, received on 18 June 1975. Receipt establishes submission chronology, not prior public circulation. The B classification records that the named author differs from the reporter; it does not mean that Brodskii developed an idea of Novikov's after the seminar. Fuchs then intervenes on Stiefel--Whitney cycles before Losik begins at the bottom of the page.

speaker: M. V. Losik
title: The affine bundle of connections and its universal connection
summary: Losik begins at the bottom of P000635 and continues through P000637. Starting from frames and a principal connection form, he constructs the finite-dimensional affine bundle whose sections are connections, then the tautological connection on the pulled-back principal bundle. Gabrielov identifies the model vector bundle. The construction predates the talk in Garc'ia's 1972 paper; a mistaken base space in the notes is corrected.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Pointed curves, pole orders and the rank-one correspondence
summary: The catalogue attributes this record to Novikov, but the dated manuscript heading on P000638 explicitly names Drinfeld (Volodya). The mathematical discussion continues through P000641. This provenance discrepancy is retained rather than silently correcting the catalogue. Gelfand and Krichever contribute curve examples and pole-order remarks; S. Gelfand gives a separate divisor explanation on P000639. The main line passes from rings of functions on a pointed curve to filtered modules and acyclic line bundles.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Divisors and the analytic Jacobian
summary: The explicitly labelled S. Gelfand intervention is the short explanation of degree-zero divisor classes at the foot of P000639. The next page labels the analytic Jacobian explanation only G.; that initial does not by itself distinguish S. I. from I. M. Gelfand. Its mathematical content is indexed here as the continuation of the explanatory intervention, with the attribution uncertainty stated. Drinfeld's filtered-module and sheaf construction, including all of P000641, remains with record 383.

speaker: V. G. Drinfeld
title: Rank-one sheaves and the tangent direction of the Jacobian flow
summary: The dated talk starts on P000642, recapitulates the filtered-module correspondence, and identifies its rank-one geometric data and Jacobian velocity. It ends in the upper portion of P000644, before the separate heading A. Polyakov. Gelfand's remark about an operator whose higher powers are differential is retained as an independent item; the later sheaf argument requires smooth function germs, a fixed leading coefficient and an acyclic initial line bundle.

speaker: A. M. Polyakov
title: Canonical quantization of Yang–Mills fields
summary: The mathematical text starts on P000644 after the conclusion of the preceding algebro-geometric discussion. Polyakov passes from the Yang--Mills Lagrangian to constrained Hamiltonian mechanics, separates longitudinal and transverse electric fields in Coulomb gauge, and proposes averaging the resulting charge kernel in the quantum vacuum. Several numerical factors and commutator signs are inconsistent in the manuscript; the reconstructed formulas below use one convention throughout. P000647 points ahead to the continuation on 5 April.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A probability distribution arising in biology
summary: A short intervention introduces what is now called the generalized Poisson distribution and sets its normalization as an exercise. The date and text are on P000648. The formula already appeared in print before this meeting; the notebook does not identify the biological model or the unnamed second example.

speaker: A. V. Roiter
title: Indecomposable modules and root systems
summary: Roiter discusses the first Brauer--Thrall theorem, chains of indecomposable submodules and a comparison of lengths. The discussion then turns to integral quadratic forms, finite and affine Dynkin diagrams, reflections and arithmetic root criteria. Kirillov's drawing of Dynkin diagrams is an intervention within this record. A final star-shaped form raises the problem of enumerating roots by reflections.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Berezin’s analysis with anticommuting variables
summary: Kirillov presents superfunctions, integration and transformations, then graded Lie algebras and a Lie correspondence. Gelfand adds a nilpotent Taylor formula. A final question asks for deformations in the direction of a Poisson bracket. The unnamed 64-dimensional algebra and its particle interpretation cannot be identified from the supplied text.

speaker: Ya. G. Sinai
title: Transfer matrices, the Ising model and square ice
summary: Sinai explains how a two-dimensional lattice partition function becomes a trace of a transfer matrix. He connects the limiting free energy to the largest eigenvalue, recalls Onsager's solution and its anticommuting-operator structure, and mentions Lieb's square-ice entropy calculation. The surviving mathematical text is on P000650.

speaker: I. M. Krichever
title: Higher-rank commuting operators; Shnirelman on spectral phases
summary: The catalogue names Krichever, but the manuscript changes speakers on P000651: Krichever and Drinfeld discuss the inverse construction of commuting ordinary differential operators, then Shnirelman discusses spectral phases, closed geodesics and the wave trace through P000653. Arnold's question about nodal sets occurs within the latter discussion. These changes are retained as speaker fields, not promoted to invented catalogue records. The first part continues the preceding algebro-geometric line; the second revisits 1973-333.18--20.

speaker: A. M. Polyakov
title: Lattice Yang–Mills fields and their partition function
summary: The continuation announced on P000647 appears on P000654. Polyakov replaces continuum connections by group-valued link variables, forms plaquette products and integrates the Boltzmann weight against product Haar measure. This is an expository return to the Wilson-lattice material of 1974-345.1--8. No new explicit confinement conjecture is written on this page.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: Computer calculations in Hamiltonian Lie-algebra cohomology
summary: Fuchs describes the polynomial cochain model, its finite weight decomposition, the exotic Gelfand--Kalinin--Fuchs classes and Perchik's constant-term Euler series. The two definite questions are to compute the whole cohomology and to prove nonvanishing of the relative Euler characteristic in unbounded weights. Buchstaber's short intervention on P000656 concerns coalgebra structures arising from multiplication and averaging. Its placement is preserved within this catalogue record. The constant-term calculation is developed with a finite, explicitly checked scope in Section~\ref{dev:perchik}.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Lorentzian geometry, Einstein’s equation and matter
summary: Novikov begins a geometrical introduction to general relativity after Buchstaber on P000656. The discussion covers the Lorentz metric, curvature, stress--energy, variational principles, perfect fluids and the Schwarzschild extension. Gelfand's question about quantizing geometry and Novikov's dimensional estimates are recorded separately from mathematical theorems. The next meeting continues this discussion in record396.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand, after L. N. Vaserstein; V. G. Drinfeld
title: Serre’s problem and Suslin’s resultant method
summary: Gelfand, following Vaserstein's notes, asks the projective-module and unimodular-row forms of Serre's problem. Drinfeld gives the monic-column reduction and Suslin's resultant translation lemma. Suslin's and Quillen's manuscripts were received before this meeting and published in 1976; no earlier public-circulation date is inferred from receipt alone. This April notebook is itself a witness to the oral transmission of Suslin's method. The earlier three-variable problem GP-1973-33 recurs in arbitrary dimension.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Relativistic fluids, coordinate freedom and Gödel’s metric
summary: The final record resumes the Einstein--fluid equations, gives the sound-speed inequalities, explains the apparent equation deficit by coordinate freedom, and mentions Gödel's closed timelike curves. The four-entry signature fixes the intended spacetime dimension despite the notation M-n. The chapter boundary follows immediately after this discussion.
